name: Equuleus
introduction: is the Little Horse, the second-smallest constellation, a tiny patch of faint stars next to the nose of Pegasus. It is one of Ptolemy’s 48 constellations, and its origins are uncertain. It is best seen on northern autumn evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Its small size hides precise timekeeping in the sky. [Delta Equulei](hip:104858), 60 light-years away, is a binary of two Sun-like stars that orbit each other every 5.7 years, one of the shortest periods known for a pair that telescopes can separate. That makes it a valuable scale for weighing stars.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Kitalpha](hip:104987), the brightest star, is a binary of a yellow giant and a white star. [Gamma Equulei](hip:104521) is a rare rapidly oscillating star with a strong magnetic field, whose brightness flickers every twelve minutes.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Small telescopes reveal several double stars in Equuleus, including Epsilon Equulei, a multiple system near the little horse’s head.
